friction_layers.title: Marcus Aurelius and Stoic Virtue
friction_layers.observation: Humans recognize the need for virtue, discipline, and self-control.
friction_layers.pattern: Character shapes the direction of the soul and life.
friction_layers.friction_point: Human beings often recognize virtue but fail to fully live by it.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Stoicism emphasizes reason, discipline, acceptance, and virtue.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity emphasizes grace, redemption through Christ, and transformation by the Holy Spirit.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: Human reason can recognize moral order, but restoration after failure requires a deeper resolution.
friction_layers.failure_risk: Do not treat Stoic virtue as identical with Christian transformation or grace.

friction_layers.title: Epictetus and Agency Under Limits
friction_layers.observation: Humans experience a real difference between what they can control and what they cannot control.
friction_layers.pattern: Moral agency grows when a person learns responsibility without pretending to control all outcomes.
friction_layers.friction_point: Acceptance can become wisdom, but it can also become resignation when suffering or injustice should be resisted.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Stoicism emphasizes disciplined judgment, inner freedom, and acceptance of what lies beyond personal control.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity emphasizes faithful agency before God, prayerful dependence, patient endurance, and justice-seeking love.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: Human agency is real but finite; the deeper resolution joins responsibility with dependence on grace and hope beyond visible control.
friction_layers.failure_risk: Do not let acceptance of limits become passivity before injustice or avoidable harm.

friction_layers.distortion: Acceptance can become wisdom, but it can also become resignation when suffering or injustice should be resisted.

friction_layers.title: Plato and the Ordered Soul
friction_layers.observation: Humans recognize that justice requires order within the person and the community.
friction_layers.pattern: The shape of the soul affects the shape of public life.
friction_layers.friction_point: A vision of order can become coercive when it ranks people by function, knowledge, or social usefulness.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Plato emphasizes philosophical reason, education, hierarchy, and the ordering of desire toward the good.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity emphasizes created dignity, servant leadership, repentance, grace, and justice for vulnerable people.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: Reason can perceive that the soul and society need order, but Christian resolution tests order by love, humility, and the dignity of every person.
friction_layers.failure_risk: Do not baptize hierarchy, philosopher-rule, or social ranking as divine order.

friction_layers.title: Aristotle and Virtue Formation
friction_layers.observation: Humans become shaped by repeated habits, practices, loves, and communities.
friction_layers.pattern: Formation turns moral insight into embodied character.
friction_layers.friction_point: Virtue can be treated as achievement, social polish, or excellence without grace for failure and repair.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Aristotle emphasizes habit, practical wisdom, moderation, friendship, and the cultivation of excellence.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity emphasizes spiritual formation, grace, repentance, sanctification, and love that is not limited to the socially excellent.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: Habit matters deeply, but Christian transformation requires more than training; it requires grace that reforms desire and restores failed persons.
friction_layers.failure_risk: Do not reduce Christian sanctification to self-cultivation or moral excellence by training alone.

friction_layers.title: Kant and Moral Duty
friction_layers.observation: Humans recognize a moral law that calls them beyond preference, appetite, and convenience.
friction_layers.pattern: Duty reveals that moral life has a claim on the self.
friction_layers.friction_point: Moral duty can identify obligation without healing the divided will or restoring the person after failure.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Kant emphasizes reason, duty, autonomy, and acting according to moral law rather than inclination.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity emphasizes moral accountability together with grace, forgiveness, union with Christ, and transformation by the Holy Spirit.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: Moral law can expose responsibility, but the deeper resolution must address guilt, weakness, forgiveness, and renewal.
friction_layers.failure_risk: Do not make moral law alone do the work of forgiveness, healing, and transformation.
sources: Immanuel Kant, Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals

friction_layers.title: Nietzsche and the Critique of Moral Weakness
friction_layers.observation: Humans can use moral language to hide fear, resentment, domination, or weakness.
friction_layers.pattern: Moral claims must be tested by what they produce in real character and community.
friction_layers.friction_point: Christian language can be misused as a mask for passivity, control, or resentment rather than cruciform love.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Nietzsche emphasizes strength, self-overcoming, suspicion of herd morality, and the creation of values.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity emphasizes the cross as power made humble, repentance from false righteousness, and Spirit-formed love that is neither domination nor resentment.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: A serious critique of moral hypocrisy can purify the pattern by forcing Christian claims to show truthful humility, courage, mercy, and costly love.
friction_layers.failure_risk: Do not use Nietzsche as support; use the critique to test whether Christian moral language has become resentment, control, or weakness.

friction_layers.title: Hume and Moral Sentiment
friction_layers.observation: Humans often make moral judgments through sympathy, feeling, habit, and social experience rather than pure reason alone.
friction_layers.pattern: Moral perception involves the whole person, not detached intellect only.
friction_layers.friction_point: If morality is grounded only in sentiment, it can struggle to name an authority beyond preference, culture, or shared feeling.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Hume emphasizes sympathy, custom, moral sentiment, and the limits of reason in human judgment.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity affirms embodied moral perception while grounding goodness in God's character, revelation, love, and the formation of rightly ordered desire.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: Moral feeling is a real part of human response, but the deeper resolution asks how desire is healed, trained, and accountable to truth.
friction_layers.failure_risk: Do not ground moral authority only in shared feeling, sympathy, or cultural habit.
sources: David Hume, An Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Morals

friction_layers.title: Marx and Religion as Social Critique
friction_layers.observation: Religion can be used to comfort suffering people without changing the unjust material conditions that harm them.
friction_layers.pattern: Claims about meaning must be tested by whether they produce justice, repair, and truthful attention to the poor.
friction_layers.friction_point: A Divine Pattern claim can become ideology if it spiritualizes suffering while leaving exploitation intact.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Marx emphasizes material conditions, class struggle, ideology critique, and social transformation through economic and political change.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity emphasizes good news to the poor, repentance from unjust power, concrete mercy, economic justice, and hope that is not reducible to material conditions.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: The pattern weakens wherever it comforts injustice; it strengthens only when worship and theology become truth-telling, mercy, justice, and repair.
friction_layers.failure_risk: Do not use spiritual language to bypass material injustice, poverty, labor exploitation, or institutional harm.

friction_layers.title: Freud and Religion as Wish-Fulfillment

friction_layers.pattern: Spiritual interpretation must be tested against projection, fear, desire, and psychological need.
friction_layers.friction_point: The Divine Pattern may be explained as human wish, coping mechanism, or unconscious projection rather than divine disclosure.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Freud emphasizes psychoanalysis, unconscious desire, illusion, and religion as a response to vulnerability and longing.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity can acknowledge projection and false religion while testing faith through revelation, repentance, truth, costly love, and transformation that resists mere wish-fulfillment.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: The pattern must distinguish genuine divine encounter from psychological projection; desire alone cannot count as evidence.
friction_layers.failure_risk: Do not treat longing, consolation, or religious experience as evidence without projection and wish-fulfillment checks.

friction_layers.title: Feuerbach and Theology as Projection
friction_layers.observation: Human beings may project their highest ideals outward and then call those ideals God.
friction_layers.pattern: Claims about God must be tested against human self-projection and idealized anthropology.
friction_layers.friction_point: The Divine Pattern may be read as humanity discovering itself rather than encountering God.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Feuerbach emphasizes religion as human nature objectified, with theology interpreted as anthropology.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity must answer projection by grounding claims in revelation, the cross, repentance, communal transformation, and a God who judges as well as fulfills human ideals.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: A pattern is weak if it only mirrors human aspiration; it must also confront, correct, and transform the human subject.
friction_layers.failure_risk: Do not confuse human ideals, moral longing, or beauty with independent evidence of divine self-disclosure.

friction_layers.title: Camus and the Absurd
friction_layers.observation: Human beings long for meaning, but the world often appears silent, unjust, and resistant to final explanation.
friction_layers.pattern: Meaning claims must survive suffering without pretending that every wound has an obvious explanation.
friction_layers.friction_point: The Divine Pattern can become morally shallow if it explains suffering too quickly or turns tragedy into neat resolution.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Camus emphasizes revolt, honesty before the absurd, solidarity, and refusing false consolation.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity emphasizes lament, the cross, resurrection hope, patient solidarity, and refusal to explain away innocent suffering.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: The pattern strengthens only when it can remain truthful in lament and avoid premature resolution.
friction_layers.failure_risk: Do not turn absurdity, grief, or innocent suffering into a tidy apologetic pattern.

friction_layers.title: Sartre and Godless Responsibility
friction_layers.observation: Human beings experience radical responsibility and cannot avoid choosing what they become.
friction_layers.pattern: Freedom requires responsibility, but responsibility can become crushing without grace or given identity.
friction_layers.friction_point: A Christian account of created purpose can be challenged as an evasion of radical freedom and human responsibility.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Sartre emphasizes existence before essence, radical freedom, responsibility, anguish, and authenticity without God.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity emphasizes created identity, responsible freedom, repentance, vocation, grace, and transformation without denying moral agency.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: The pattern must preserve real human responsibility while showing why freedom is gift and vocation, not mere self-invention.
friction_layers.failure_risk: Do not use divine purpose to erase human agency, responsibility, or the terror of real choice.

friction_layers.title: Darwin and Natural Selection
friction_layers.observation: Complex life can arise through natural processes involving variation, inheritance, selection, adaptation, contingency, and deep time.
friction_layers.pattern: Claims about creation must account for natural history without forcing biological complexity into simple proof of design.
friction_layers.friction_point: Natural selection challenges easy design arguments and any Divine Pattern claim that depends on biological complexity being inexplicable by natural causes.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Darwinian explanation emphasizes descent with modification and natural selection as a powerful account of biological diversity.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity can treat creation as sustained gift and providence without denying natural mechanisms, contingency, creaturely suffering, or scientific explanation.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: The pattern must not compete with biology; it must ask theological questions at the level of gift, order, contingency, vocation, and creaturely care.
friction_layers.failure_risk: Do not use gaps in evolutionary explanation as evidence for the Divine Pattern.
sources: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species
Charles Darwin, The Descent of Man
friction_layers.source_review_note: Add qualified science-source review, avoid gaps-based reasoning, and identify the theological claim that remains after natural explanation is honored.

friction_layers.title: Foucault and Power-Knowledge
friction_layers.observation: Institutions can produce truth-claims that discipline bodies, normalize behavior, and protect power.
friction_layers.pattern: Truth claims must be tested by how they shape people, especially vulnerable bodies and communities.
friction_layers.friction_point: The Divine Pattern framework can become a tool of classification and control if it names patterns without checking power.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Foucault emphasizes genealogy, power-knowledge, discipline, normalization, and suspicion toward institutions that claim neutral truth.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity emphasizes truth joined to humility, repentance, protection of the vulnerable, servant authority, and the cross as judgment on coercive power.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: The pattern must audit its own power effects; truth without humility and repair can become domination.
friction_layers.failure_risk: Do not let pattern recognition become surveillance, labeling, normalization, or institutional self-protection.
